scenes.text: Ten years of evidence on health and heat, in eight numbers.
Seven hundred and ten thousand deaths linked to heat in 2023, a record. Thirteen and a half heatwave days per person in 2025, eleven of them added by climate change.
Five hundred and seventy-three billion work hours lost, a trillion dollars of income, and forty-eight hours of sleep a year, per person.

Air conditioning may have prevented three hundred and sixty thousand deaths a year. Forty-six countries warn for heat-related illness. And health needs of three point three billion dollars a year met about a third.
What they mean for South and Southeast Asia, and for you.
